'''Bruce Wallace''' (18 May 1920 – 12 January 2015) was an American scientist. He was University Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Biological Sciences at [[Virginia Tech]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=In memoriam: Bruce Wallace, University Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Biological Sciences |url=https://vtx.vt.edu/content/vtx_vt_edu/en/articles/2015/01/012315-science-wallacememoriam.html |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=vtx.vt.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Wallace was born and raised in [[McKean, Pennsylvania]]. He received his bachelor's degree in zoology from [[Columbia University]] before joining the [[United States Army]]. He served as a statistical control officer under [[Robert McNamara]] before returning to Columbia to earn his doctoral degree in 1949, studying under [[Theodosius Dobzhansky]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Bruce Wallace Obituary (2015) Ithaca Journal |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/theithacajournal/name/bruce-wallace-obituary?id=22487372 |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref> He joined the [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]] in 1947 and was promoted to its assistant director. In 1958, he joined the faculty of [[Cornell University]] and held the position of professor of genetics until 1981 to become University Distinguished Professor of Biology at Virginia Tech.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Distinguished geneticist Bruce Wallace dies at 94 |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2015/02/distinguished-geneticist-bruce-wallace-dies-94 |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=Cornell Chronicle |language=en}}</ref> Wallace retired from teaching in 1994. His research has initially focused on the study of genetics and natural populations, but shifted towards environmental issues after his retirement.

Among his contributions to the field of biology was his conceptualization of an "island machine" to estimate the equilibrium number of species in the biogeography of a laboratory island and the major determinant of extinction.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wallace |first=Bruce |date=1975 |title=The Biogeography of Laboratory Islands |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2407073 |journal=Evolution |volume=29 |issue=4 |pages=622–635 |doi=10.2307/2407073 |jstor=2407073 |pmid=28563100 |issn=0014-3820|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He also anticipated the structure and roles of enhancers in [[gene regulation]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wallace |first1=Bruce |last2=Kass |first2=Thomas L. |date=July 1974 |title=On the Structure of Gene Control Regions |journal=Genetics |volume=77 |issue=3 |pages=541–558 |doi=10.1093/genetics/77.3.541 |issn=0016-6731 |pmc=1213146 |pmid=4414920}}</ref>

Wallace was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1970.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bruce Wallace |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/bruce-wallace-m7zf60/ |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> However, he resigned from the academy after learning that through its operating arm, the [[National Research Council (United States)|National Research Council]], had committees doing secret war research funded by the [[United States Department of Defense]] during the [[Vietnam War]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |date=2015-05-01 |title=In Memory of Bruce Wallace: 1920–2015 |journal=Journal of Heredity |volume=106 |issue=3 |pages=331–332 |doi=10.1093/jhered/esv024 |pmid=26086052 |issn=0022-1503|doi-access=free |last1=MacIntyre |first1=R. J. |last2=Gearhart |first2=J. D. |last3=Effron |first3=J. W. |last4=O' Brien |first4=S. J. |last5=Fogleman |first5=J. }}</ref> He was reinstated in the academy after the war was over.

He was also a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bruce Wallace |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/bruce-wallace |access-date=2022-06-14 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |language=en}}</ref> Wallace served as president of numerous learned societies, including the [[Genetics Society of America]], the [[American Society of Naturalists]], the [[Society for the Study of Evolution]], and the [[American Genetic Association|American Genetics Association]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bruce Wallace |url=https://cpb-us-e1.wpmucdn.com/blogs.cornell.edu/dist/3/6798/files/2016/01/WALLACE-Bruce-23all8g.pdf |access-date=June 14, 2022}}</ref>

He died on 12 January 2015, in [[Blacksburg, Virginia]], at age 94.<ref name=":1" />
